  • Method Details

    • print

      String print()
      Returns a human-readable representation of the automaton.
      Returns:
      table containing states, state types and transitions

    • deterministic

      boolean deterministic()
      Checks whether the automaton is deterministic.
      Returns:
      true if there are no epsilon transitions and no state has more than one outgoing transition with the same symbol

    • empty

      boolean empty()
      Checks whether the language of the automaton is empty.
      Returns:
      true if no final state is reachable from the start state

    • recognize

      boolean recognize(String word)
      Checks whether the automaton accepts the given word.
      Parameters:
      word - word to test; the empty word is represented by the empty string
      Returns:
      true if the word is accepted by the automaton

    • concat

      Automaton concat(Automaton a)
      Creates a new automaton for the concatenation of this automaton and another one.
      Parameters:
      a - automaton to concatenate after this automaton
      Returns:
      automaton accepting the concatenated language

    • union

      Automaton union(Automaton a)
      Creates a new automaton for the union of this automaton and another one.
      Parameters:
      a - automaton to unite with this automaton
      Returns:
      automaton accepting words from either language

    • un

      Automaton un()
      Creates a new automaton for the positive closure of this automaton. Positive closure is also known as Kleene plus and means one or more repetitions.
      Returns:
      automaton accepting one or more repetitions of the original language
